title: Diagnose rear-halfshaft noises and vibration
introduction:
Begin with when the symptom happens, not with a guess at the part. A clunk while changing direction, a grunt as the car starts moving and a vibration at cruising speed lead to different checks. The halfshafts carry torque from the differential to the rear wheels, while their constant-velocity joints accommodate suspension movement.

Use the inspection list first. Then match the reproduced symptom to its row in the chart and follow that row’s cause and action together. A possible cause in the table is a test direction, not an automatic replacement order.

edits.text: Understand the driveline connection
Confirm the symptom and inspect
Confirm the reported concern by establishing what happens and when it occurs.
edits.why: Useful distinctions include a direction change, moving away from a stop and cruising at speed.

edits.text: Look for visible mechanical damage and other obvious problems.
edits.why: Start with the parts listed below before moving into symptom-specific checks.

edits.text: Visual inspection points
Loose hardware
edits.why: Check whether the visible connections are secure.

edits.text: Constant velocity (CV) joint boot(s)
edits.why: The boots protect the joints; look for obvious boot damage.

edits.text: CV joint(s)
edits.why: Inspect the joints for visible damage.

edits.text: Rear drive halfshaft(s)
edits.why: Inspect the shafts themselves as well as their joints.

edits.text: If you find an obvious cause that explains the reported or observed symptom, correct it where possible before continuing to the next step.
edits.why: A directly observed fault should be addressed before a more involved diagnostic path.

edits.text: If the cause is not apparent from the visual inspection, confirm the symptom and continue to the Symptom Chart.
edits.why: Keep the operating condition with the symptom so you select the appropriate row.

edits.text: Choose the symptom that matches
Driveline clunk: a loud clunk when changing from REVERSE to DRIVE.
Possible cause: a damaged or worn CV joint.
Inspect the CV joints for wear or damage. Replace the rear drive halfshaft if the inspection shows it is necessary. Use [Rear Halfshaft (205-05)](#/document/G2214772).
edits.why: Replacement depends on the inspection finding, not the sound alone.

edits.text: Driveline clunk: a clunk as the vehicle begins moving forward after a stop.
Possible cause: a loose hub nut.
Check the hub-nut torque. If it is outside specification, install a new hub nut. Use [Rear Halfshaft (205-05)](#/document/G2214772) for the hub-nut instructions and specification.
edits.why: This branch requires a new nut when the measured torque is not to specification.

edits.text: Grunting: usually heard with a shudder during acceleration from a complete stop.
Possible cause: a rear-halfshaft CV joint that binds.
Check that the outer CV joint is correctly seated in the hub, and repair as needed using [Rear Halfshaft (205-05)](#/document/G2214772).
edits.why: This check concerns the joint’s seating at the hub.

edits.text: Driveline vibration: vibration occurring at cruising speeds.
Possible cause: a binding or damaged rear-halfshaft CV joint.
Check the outer CV joint for correct seating in the hub. Repair as needed using [Rear Halfshaft (205-05)](#/document/G2214772).
edits.why: Follow this row for the cruising-speed symptom rather than borrowing a different row’s replacement instruction.

edits.text: Protect the halfshaft seals during installation
NOTICE: Keep the halfshaft splines from touching the rear drive halfshaft seals during installation. Contact with the splines can damage the seals.

Incorrect installation can damage a rear halfshaft seal in the same ways it can damage a drive pinion seal. Keep the seal bore clean, and handle the sealing lip carefully so it is not cut or torn. The surface the seal runs against must have no nicks, gouges or rough texture.
edits.why: A new seal still needs an undamaged mating surface and careful installation.

edits.text: For rear halfshaft seal installation, use [Rear Halfshaft Seal (205-02)](#/document/G2214752).
